text: The north side of town, under the keep. Stone houses with slate roofs line its lanes, built by the lord's masons and the families who serve the castle.
The east side of town, round the square and the church. Merchants build tall here, timber floors jutting over the street above a stone shop at the ground.
The south and west of town, toward the river road. Smiths, dyers and coopers keep workshops in the yards behind their houses, and the smoke hangs low at dusk.
Cottages and smithies along the east road, past the moat bridge. They grew outside the wall, where rents were low and the noisier trades were allowed.
The south road's houses down to the river bridge, with the mill on the bank. They grew outside the wall, where rents were low and the noisier trades were allowed.
Cottages and gardens strung along the west road. They grew outside the wall, where rents were low and the noisier trades were allowed.
